readings: Taps at bit positions 5 and 3 are 1-indexed from LSB, so they correspond to q[4] (MSB) and q[2] (middle bit).
Taps are 0-indexed, but position 5 is invalid in a 5-bit register; a reasonable engineer may instead use q[3] and q[1] or number bits from MSB giving q[0] and q[2].
The XOR with q[0] is applied to the shifted-in value at the tap position (standard Galois): next q[i] = (shifted-in value) XOR q[0].
The XOR with q[0] is applied to the current bit before shifting: next state = (q XOR (q[0] ? mask : 0)) >> 1.
